title.en: King Xiao of Zhou appoints Feizi to raise horses between the Qian and Wei rivers

summary.en: To revitalize the royal army, King Xiao of Zhou established a pasture at the confluence of the Qian and Wei rivers (present-day Baoji, Shaanxi) and appointed Feizi, a leader of the Ying clan, to manage horse breeding. Feizi excelled at horse husbandry, greatly increasing the number and quality of horses. In reward, King Xiao granted Feizi the land of Qin (present-day Tianshui,

statement.zh: 周孝王为振兴王室军力，在汧水与渭水之间的交汇处（今陕西宝鸡一带）设立牧场，命嬴姓首领非子负责养马。非子善于畜马，马匹数量大增且质量优良，周孝王因此将秦地（今甘肃天水）封给非子作为附庸，准许其在秦地建立城邑，延续嬴姓祭祀。这一事件是秦国受封的滥觞，为日后秦人崛起奠定了物质基础。
statement.en:
To revitalize the royal army, King Xiao of Zhou established a pasture at the confluence of the Qian and Wei rivers (present-day Baoji, Shaanxi) and appointed Feizi, a leader of the Ying clan, to manage horse breeding. Feizi excelled at horse husbandry, greatly increasing the number and quality of horses. In reward, King Xiao granted Feizi the land of Qin (present-day Tianshui, Gansu) as a dependent state, allowing him to build a city there and continue the Ying clan's sacrifices. This event marked the beginning of the Qin state's enfeoffment and laid the material foundation for the eventual rise of the Qin people.

For Asia in 899 BCE, “King Xiao of Zhou appoints Feizi to raise horses between the Qian and Wei rivers” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Egyptian Pharaoh Osorkon I stabilizes the Nile Delta

summary.en: Osorkon I (r. c. 922–887 BCE) of Egypt's 22nd Dynasty strengthened central authority in the Nile Delta by appointing Libyan relatives as governors of nomes (provinces), successfully quelling rebellions by the Amun priesthood in Thebes. He undertook major construction at Bubastis, building a large temple dedicated to the cat goddess Bastet, and gained priestly support through do

statement.zh: 埃及第二十二王朝法老奥索尔孔一世（Osorkon I，约前922-前887年在位）在尼罗河三角洲地区强化中央集权，通过任命利比亚裔亲族担任各诺姆（州）总督，有效平息了底比斯地区的阿蒙神庙势力叛乱。他在布巴斯提斯（Bubastis）大兴土木，建造了规模宏大的庙宇献给猫神芭丝特，并以金银器捐献获得祭司阶层的支持。暂时延缓了埃及的分裂趋势。
statement.en: The Pharaoh of the 22nd Dynasty of Egypt, Osorkon I (reigned approximately 922-887 BCE), strengthened centralization of power in the Nile Delta region and effectively quelled the rebellion of the Temple of Amun forces in Thebes by appointing Libyan relatives as governors of various Nomes (states).

title.en: King Xiao of Zhou reorganizes eastern defense lines by enfeoffing vassals

title.en: King Yi of Zhou dies; King Xiao of Zhou, Ji Pifang, ascends the throne

summary.en: King Yi of Zhou (Ji Jian) died. statement.zh: 西周第八位君主周懿王姬囏去世，因其太子姬燮懦弱无能，身为叔父的姬辟方在贵族支持下夺取王位，是为周孝王。这次继位打破了周朝嫡长子继承制，引起部分诸侯不满。孝王即位后，首先平定西境戎狄的骚扰，并试图通过改革王室马政来重振军力，反映了西周中期王室权威的衰落与内部权力斗争。
statement.en:
King Yi of Zhou (Ji Jian) died. Because his crown prince Ji Xie was considered weak and incompetent, the king's uncle Ji Pifang seized the throne with support from nobles, becoming King Xiao of Zhou. This succession violated the Zhou primogeniture system and displeased some vassals. After ascending, King Xiao first pacified disturbances by the Rong tribes in the west and attempted to reform royal horse administration to revive military strength, reflecting the decline of royal authority and internal power struggles in the mid-Western Zhou.

For Asia in 892 BCE, “King Yi of Zhou dies; King Xiao of Zhou, Ji Pifang, ascends the throne” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Assyrian king Tukulti-Ninurta II begins full conquest of Nairi

summary.en: Assyrian king Tukulti-Ninurta II assembled a large army and launched a full-scale conquest of the Nairi region. statement.en:
Western Rong tribes invaded Zhou's western borders. King Xiao ordered the Marquis of Shen to lead a counterattack. The Marquis of Shen, in coordination with the Ying clan leader Daluo of Quanqiu (present-day Tianshui, Gansu), decisively defeated the Western Rong on the upper Wei River, capturing their leader and seizing 10,000 of livestock. This victory stabilized the northwestern frontier, and King Xiao enfeoffed Daluo's son as formal lord of Quanqiu, strengthening the alliance between the Zhou and the Ying clan.

statement.zh: 周孝王姬辟方去世，因孝王无强势子嗣，懿王太子姬燮在贵族和诸侯拥立下继位，是为周夷王。夷王性格软弱，即位初期便受到王室卿士和诸侯的牵制。为挽回王威，夷王一反传统下堂接见诸侯，开启了周王对诸侯过分礼遇的先例，从此天子权威进一步下降，诸侯开始骄横不朝。
statement.en:
King Xiao of Zhou (Ji Pifang) died. As Xiao had no strong heir, Crown Prince Ji Xie, son of King Yi, was enthroned with support from nobles and vassals, becoming King Yi of Zhou. Yi was weak-willed and was immediately constrained by royal ministers and vassals. In an attempt to restore royal prestige, Yi broke tradition by descending from the hall to receive vassals, setting a precedent of excessive courtesy toward vassals. From then on, royal authority declined further, and vassals became increasingly arrogant and disobedient.

For Asia in 886 BCE, “King Xiao of Zhou dies; King Yi of Zhou, Ji Xie, ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

sources.excerpt: The annals of Ashurnasirpal II give a detailed account of the campaigns of his first six years as king and show him moving from one corner of his empire to another, putting down rebellions, reorganizing provinces, exacting tribute, and meeting opposition with calculated ruthlessness. statement.en:
King Yi of Zhou (Ji Xie) died, and his son Ji Hu succeeded as King Li of Zhou. Having witnessed his father's loss of authority and the arrogance of vassals from a young age, Li was determined to restore royal power. However, he was cruel and greedy. Soon after ascending, he began implementing exploitative fiscal policies, such as monopolizing mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes. He appointed Rong Yigong as a minister, attempting to deprive the common people of their livelihood from natural resources, which intensified conflicts with nobles and commoners and laid the groundwork for the later 'uprising of the commoners'.

For Asia in 878 BCE, “King Yi of Zhou dies; King Li of Zhou, Ji Hu, ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

Osorkon II of Egypt's 22nd Dynasty was crowned at Bubastis. He faced rebellion from provincial governors in the eastern Delta and the growing independence of the Amun priesthood at Thebes. title.en: King Ahab of Israel strengthens trade cooperation with Tyre

title.en: Gadir (Cádiz) becomes the Phoenician gateway to the Atlantic

summary.en: In the ninth century BCE Tyrians developed Gadir on a chain of sandbars off southwestern Iberia; the earliest Phoenician pottery and buildings found at Cádiz date from this period. The site stood on a headland behind a natural harbour, commanding the Atlantic side of the Strait of Gibraltar. The Phoenicians traded eastern oil, wine, painted pottery and textiles for the silver a

statement.zh: 公元前9世纪，推罗人在伊比利亚半岛西南的一串沙洲上经营加迪尔，此地出土的最早腓尼基陶器与建筑遗存即属此时。城址踞海角而立，背靠天然避风港，扼直布罗陀海峡外侧的大西洋出口。腓尼基人以东方的油、酒、彩陶与纺织品，交换当地塔尔提索斯人的白银和铜——瓜达尔基维尔河下游的银矿是当时地中海世界最大的白银来源之一，源源流向推罗，用以偿付亚述的贡赋。加迪尔更是通往北方锡矿与西非黄金的中转站，腓尼基船只由此沿大西洋岸南北航行。城中的麦勒卡特神庙香火1000年不绝，罗马人称之为"赫拉克勒斯神庙"，汉尼拔出征意大利前曾专程前来献祭。
statement.en:
In the ninth century BCE Tyrians developed Gadir on a chain of sandbars off southwestern Iberia; the earliest Phoenician pottery and buildings found at Cádiz date from this period. The site stood on a headland behind a natural harbour, commanding the Atlantic side of the Strait of Gibraltar. The Phoenicians traded eastern oil, wine, painted pottery and textiles for the silver and copper of the local Tartessians—the mines of the lower Guadalquivir were among the greatest sources of silver in the Mediterranean world, and the metal flowed to Tyre to pay Assyrian tribute. Gadir was also the staging point for northern tin and West African gold, with Phoenician ships working the Atlantic coast in both directions. Its temple of Melqart remained in use for a thousand years; the Romans called it the temple of Hercules, and Hannibal sacrificed there before setting out for Italy.

For Europe in 870 BCE, “Gadir (Cádiz) becomes the Phoenician gateway to the Atlantic” is a traceable node of Economy change whose significance is best read through later events.

summary.en: Conflicts between Pharaoh Osorkon II of Egypt and the Amun priesthood at Thebes escalated. statement.zh: 埃及法老奥索尔孔二世与底比斯阿蒙祭司集团矛盾升级，祭司拒绝承认法老的权威，法老则派军南下洗劫了部分卡纳克神庙的财产。底比斯城爆发平民起义，法老被迫妥协，重新任命祭司长。这一事件暴露了埃及中央政府已无力控制南方，底比斯实际上成为半独立的神权国家。
statement.en:
Conflicts between Pharaoh Osorkon II of Egypt and the Amun priesthood at Thebes escalated. The priests refused to recognize the pharaoh's authority, and the pharaoh sent troops south to loot part of the Karnak Temple treasury. A popular uprising broke out in Thebes, forcing the pharaoh to compromise and reappoint the high priest. This event revealed that the Egyptian central government could no longer control the south, and Thebes effectively became a semi-independent theocratic state.

For Africa in 869 BCE, “Internal conflict intensifies in Egypt's 22nd Dynasty” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: King Li of Zhou orders Nangong Shi to attack E

summary.en: Marquis E Yufang allied with the Huaiyi and rebelled again. King Li ordered Nangong Shi to lead the Western Six Armies and the Eastern Eight Armies against E. The royal forces defeated the E army in the Han River valley, captured Marquis E Yufang, and presented him at the ancestral Zhou capital. E's territory was incorporated into the royal domain. The bronze 'Yu Ding' inscript

statement.zh: 鄂侯驭方联合淮夷再次反叛，周厉王命令南宫氏率领西六师和殷八师讨伐鄂国。王师在汉水流域击败鄂军，俘获鄂侯驭方并献于宗周，鄂国土地被并入王室直辖。青铜器“禹鼎”铭文详细记载了此次战事，并提到周军使用了数千匹战马，反映了西周晚期军事动员的庞大规模和厉王初期军事上的成功。
statement.en:
Marquis E Yufang allied with the Huaiyi and rebelled again. King Li ordered Nangong Shi to lead the Western Six Armies and the Eastern Eight Armies against E. The royal forces defeated the E army in the Han River valley, captured Marquis E Yufang, and presented him at the ancestral Zhou capital. E's territory was incorporated into the royal domain. The bronze 'Yu Ding' inscription records this campaign in detail, mentioning the use of several thousand war horses, reflecting the large scale of military mobilization in the late Western Zhou and King Li's early military successes.

For Asia in 861 BCE, “King Li of Zhou orders Nangong Shi to attack E” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Shalmaneser III occupies the ports of Tyre and Sidon

summary.en: Shalmaneser III marched to the eastern Mediterranean coast. The Phoenician city-states of Tyre, Sidon, and Byblos submitted and paid tribute to avoid war. Assyrian forces did not enter the city-states but occupied the surrounding farmland and controlled port revenues. The king of Tyre offered 120 talents (about 3.6 tons) of silver, along with cedar wood, ivory, and purple cloth

statement.zh: 沙缦以色三世率军抵达地中海东岸，腓尼基城邦提尔、西顿和毕布勒斯纷纷纳贡以避免战争。亚述军队并未攻入城邦内部，而是占领了周边农业区并控制港口税收。提尔国王提供120塔兰特（约3.6吨）白银的贡品，以及雪松木、象牙和紫色布料，亚述以书面形式确认了城邦的内部自治，开启了亚述与腓尼基的附庸关系。
statement.en:
Shalmaneser III marched to the eastern Mediterranean coast. The Phoenician city-states of Tyre, Sidon, and Byblos submitted and paid tribute to avoid war. Assyrian forces did not enter the city-states but occupied the surrounding farmland and controlled port revenues. The king of Tyre offered 120 talents (about 3.6 tons) of silver, along with cedar wood, ivory, and purple cloth. Assyria confirmed the city-states' internal autonomy in writing, establishing a vassal relationship between Assyria and Phoenicia.

For Asia in 858 BCE, “Shalmaneser III occupies the ports of Tyre and Sidon” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 犹太国王约兰（Jehoram，约前849-前842年在位）娶以色列国王亚哈与耶洗别之女亚他利雅（Athaliah）为妻。亚他利雅将巴力崇拜引入耶路撒冷，建立巴力神庙，并说服约兰杀害了犹太王室中敬拜雅威的多数成员。这导致犹太国陷入宗教混乱，先知以利亚为此发出谴责，预言王室将遭灾祸。
statement.en:
Jehoram (r. c. 849–842 BCE), king of Judah, married Athaliah, daughter of King Ahab of Israel and Jezebel. Athaliah introduced Baal worship into Jerusalem, built a temple for Baal, and persuaded Jehoram to kill most of the members of the Judean royal house who worshipped Yahweh. This plunged Judah into religious turmoil, and the prophet Elijah condemned the actions, prophesying disaster for the royal family.

For Asia in 857 BCE, “King Jehoram of Judah marries Athaliah, introducing Baal worship” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 沙缦以色三世首次进攻大马士革城，该城由亚兰国王便哈达二世坚固防守。亚述军队使用攻城塔和破城锤猛攻一个月，但大马士革的高大城墙和防守者的火油反击令亚述伤亡惨重。由于雨季来临和补给困难，沙缦以色三世被迫撤军。此次失败并未动摇亚述霸权，但鼓励了叙利亚诸国组建更强大的反亚述联盟。
statement.en:
Shalmaneser III attacked Damascus for the first time. The city was strongly defended by Aramean king Ben-Hadad II. Assyrian forces used siege towers and battering rams for a month, but Damascus's high walls and defenders' use of flaming oil caused heavy Assyrian casualties. With the rainy season approaching and supply difficulties, Shalmaneser III was forced to withdraw. This failure did not undermine Assyrian hegemony but encouraged Syrian states to form a stronger anti-Assyrian coalition.

For Asia in 856 BCE, “Shalmaneser III fails to capture Damascus” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: King Li of Zhou increases military pressure on the Huaiyi

summary.en: Huaiyi tribes allied to raid Zhou's southeastern borders, looting grain and copper materials. King Li sent Guozhong with the Chengzhou Eight Armies eastward. They defeated the Huaiyi coalition on the north bank of the Huai River, capturing their leaders and seizing large quantities of copper ingots. This victory temporarily restored the security of the 'metal and tin route' (co

statement.zh: 淮夷部落联合骚扰周朝东南边境，掠夺粮食和青铜原料。周厉王派遣虢仲率领成周八师东征，在淮水北岸击败淮夷联军，擒获其首领并缴获大量铜锭。这次胜利使周朝短暂恢复了“金道锡行”（铜锡运输路线）的安全，青铜铸造得以继续进行，但淮夷的威胁并未彻底解除。
statement.en:
Huaiyi tribes allied to raid Zhou's southeastern borders, looting grain and copper materials. King Li sent Guozhong with the Chengzhou Eight Armies eastward. They defeated the Huaiyi coalition on the north bank of the Huai River, capturing their leaders and seizing large quantities of copper ingots. This victory temporarily restored the security of the 'metal and tin route' (copper-tin transport route), allowing bronze casting to continue, but the Huaiyi threat was not completely eliminated.

statement.en:
Assyrian king Shalmaneser III faced a 12-king coalition led by Ben-Hadad II of Damascus and King Ahab of Israel at Qarqar in northern Syria. According to Assyrian inscriptions, the coalition had about 3,900 chariots, 2,000 cavalry, and 50,000 infantry; Assyria fielded about 20,000 infantry and 1,200 chariots. After a fierce day of fighting, both sides suffered heavy losses. Assyria failed to break the coalition, but the coalition could not counterattack. statement.zh: 先知以利沙派门徒膏立将军耶户（Jehu）为以色列王。耶户随即发动政变，先后杀死以色列王约兰和犹太王亚哈谢，并追击亚哈的母亲耶洗别。王后耶洗别被从窗户扔下摔死，狗吃了她的尸体。耶户接着屠杀了亚哈家族的70个子孙和所有巴力先知，拆毁巴力庙，以极端手段推翻暗利王朝并恢复雅威崇拜，但此举也导致以色列与腓尼基和犹太的关系破裂。

The prophet Elisha sent a disciple to anoint Jehu as king of Israel. Jehu led a coup, killing King Joram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah, then pursuing Jezebel, the mother of Ahab. Jehu then massacred 70 descendants of the house of Ahab and all the prophets of Baal, demolished the temple of Baal, and restored the worship of Yahweh by extreme means, ending the Omride dynasty. title.en: King Jehoram of Judah suppresses Edomite rebellion

summary.en: Jehoram, king of Judah, led his army to Edom to suppress the long-rebellious Edomites. Edom had the important port of Elath on the Gulf of Aqaba. statement.zh: 犹太国王约兰（Jehoram）率军前往以东，镇压长期反叛的以东人。以东在亚喀巴湾沿岸有重要港口以旬迦别（Elath），犹太军队一度收复该港，但以东人采取游击战术迫使犹太军撤退。约兰未能彻底平定以东，犹太从此失去对红海贸易路线的控制，财政收入严重受损。

Jehoram, king of Judah, led his army to Edom to suppress the long-rebellious Edomites. Edom had the important port of Elath on the Gulf of Aqaba. The Judean army temporarily recaptured the port, but the Edomites used guerrilla tactics to force their retreat. statement.en:
The Xianyun tribes (one of the ancestors of the Xiongnu) from the northwest invaded Zhou territory. King Li ordered Guozhong to lead a large army against them. title.en: Jehu of Israel submits to Assyrian king Shalmaneser III as vassal

The Black Obelisk inscription records that Jehu (or his envoy) brought tribute of gold, silver, tin, lead, and ivory. The Assyrian king did not demand the abolition of Israel's religious independence. This diplomatic policy temporarily spared

statement.zh: 以色列国王耶户在清洗亚哈家族后，为稳固政权和对抗大马士革，主动向亚述王沙缦以色三世称臣。黑色方尖碑铭文记载，耶户（或他的使者）带来了金银、锡、铅和象牙作为贡品，亚述王没有要求以色列取消宗教独立。这一外交政策使以色列暂时避免了亚述的直接攻击，但成了亚述的附庸国。
statement.en:
Jehu, king of Israel, after purging the house of Ahab, voluntarily submitted to Shalmaneser III to secure his rule and counter Damascus. The Black Obelisk inscription records that Jehu (or his envoy) brought tribute of gold, silver, tin, lead, and ivory. The Assyrian king did not demand the abolition of Israel's religious independence. This diplomatic policy temporarily spared Israel from direct Assyrian attack but made it an Assyrian vassal.

summary.en: Shalmaneser III launched his ninth campaign against stubborn Damascus, destroying all villages, gardens, and irrigation works outside the city. statement.zh: 沙缦以色三世对顽固的大马士革发动第九次战役，摧毁了城外所有村庄、花园和水利设施，并用攻城锤连续轰击外城墙两个月，最终攻破外城。大马士革国王哈薛（Hazael）退守内城，利用储藏的粮食和弓箭手继续抵抗。由于严冬和瘟疫，亚述再次撤军，但大马士革已元气大伤，国土大半荒芜。
statement.en:
Shalmaneser III launched his ninth campaign against stubborn Damascus, destroying all villages, gardens, and irrigation works outside the city. He used battering rams continuously for two months against the outer wall and finally breached it. King Hazael of Damascus withdrew to the inner city, using stored food and archers to continue resistance. Due to harsh winter and plague, Assyria again withdrew, but Damascus was greatly weakened, most of its land devastated.

For Asia in 842 BCE, “Shalmaneser III destroys outer wall of Damascus, besieges inner city” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Popular uprising; King Li of Zhou flees to Zhi

summary.en: Due to King Li's long-standing 'exclusive rights' policy and suppression of speech, the commoners and lower nobility in Haojing were unable to bear it any longer. They spontaneously gathered, armed with sticks, and surrounded the palace. King Li fled hastily with his close followers, crossed the Yellow River, and escaped to Zhi (present-day Huozhou, Shanxi), where he died. Crow

statement.zh: 因周厉王连年推行“专利”政策并压制言论，镐京的国人和中小贵族忍无可忍，自发集结起来手持棍棒围攻王宫。厉王带领亲信仓皇出逃，渡过黄河逃到彘地（今山西霍州），终老于此。太子姬静藏在召穆公家中，暴民包围召公家要求交出太子，召公用自己的儿子代替太子交给暴民，太子得以幸存。厉王出奔标志着西周王权的一次严重崩溃。
statement.en:
Due to King Li's long-standing 'exclusive rights' policy and suppression of speech, the commoners and lower nobility in Haojing were unable to bear it any longer. They spontaneously gathered, armed with sticks, and surrounded the palace. King Li fled hastily with his close followers, crossed the Yellow River, and escaped to Zhi (present-day Huozhou, Shanxi), where he died. Crown Prince Jing hid in the home of Duke Mu of Shao. The rioters surrounded Duke Mu's house and demanded the prince. Duke Mu gave his own son to the mob in place of the prince, saving the prince's life. The king's flight marked a severe collapse of Western Zhou royal authority.

For Asia in 841 BCE, “Popular uprising; King Li of Zhou flees to Zhi” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Jehu's coup in Israel ends the Omride dynasty

summary.en: Jehu, an Israelite general, launched a military coup at Ramoth-gilead, killing King Joram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah. statement.zh: 以色列将军耶户在基列的拉末发动军事政变，杀死以色列王约兰和犹大王亚哈谢，接着在耶斯列将王后耶洗别摔死。耶户随后血洗了亚哈家族的70个子孙和所有巴力先知，彻底消灭了暗利王朝。耶户自立为王，开启耶户王朝，并摧毁巴力庙，回归雅威崇拜。但耶户的极端手段导致以色列与推罗和犹大关系决裂，国力严重受损。
statement.en:
Jehu, an Israelite general, launched a military coup at Ramoth-gilead, killing King Joram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah. He then had Queen Jezebel thrown from a window in Jezreel to her death, where dogs ate her body. Jehu massacred 70 descendants of the house of Ahab and all the prophets of Baal, completely ending the Omride dynasty. Jehu declared himself king, beginning the Jehu dynasty. He destroyed the temple of Baal and returned to the worship of Yahweh. However, his extreme measures broke Israel's relations with Tyre and Judah, severely weakening the kingdom.

title.en: Earliest open-air theater prototype appears in Greece

summary.en: Near Miletus, archaeologists have found traces of stone benches arranged in rows on a slope, interpreted as early theaters for communal rituals and choral performances. These circular or semi-circular spaces could hold several hundred people, where poets recited the Homeric epics and hymns were performed at festivals of Dionysus. The emergence of theater laid the foundation for

statement.zh: 在希腊的米利都附近，考古发现了斜坡上排列整齐的石凳遗迹，被认为是用于集体祭祀和合唱表演的早期剧场。这种圆形或半圆形空间可容纳数百人，诗人在这里吟诵荷马史诗，酒神节上演出颂歌。戏剧雏形的出现为希腊古典时代伟大的悲剧和喜剧奠定了基础，并反映了城邦公共生活的活跃化。
statement.en:
Near Miletus, archaeologists have found traces of stone benches arranged in rows on a slope, interpreted as early theaters for communal rituals and choral performances. These circular or semi-circular spaces could hold several 100 people, where poets recited the Homeric epics and hymns were performed at festivals of Dionysus. The emergence of theater laid the foundation for the great tragedies and comedies of classical Greece and reflected the burgeoning public life of the city-states.

title.en: Jehu of Israel dies; Jehoahaz succeeds

summary.en: Jehu, king of Israel, died, and his son Jehoahaz succeeded. Jehoahaz faced continuous aggression from Aram (Damascus). Israel lost all territories east of the Jordan River, and the army was reduced to only 50 cavalry, 10 chariots, and 10,000 infantry. Jehoahaz prayed to God and received temporary peace, but Israel became a vassal of Aram, and its power hit a low point.

statement.zh: 以色列国王耶户去世，其子约哈斯（Jehoahaz）即位。约哈斯面临亚兰（大马士革）的持续侵略，以色列丧失了约旦河以东所有领土，军队被缩减到仅剩50名骑兵、10辆战车和10000名步兵。约哈斯向上帝祈求，获得了暂时的和平，但以色列沦为亚兰的附庸国，国力跌至低谷。
statement.en:
Jehu, king of Israel, died, and his son Jehoahaz succeeded. Jehoahaz faced continuous aggression from Aram (Damascus). Israel lost all territories east of the Jordan River, and the army was reduced to only 50 cavalry, 10 chariots, and 10,000 infantry. Jehoahaz prayed to God and received temporary peace, but Israel became a vassal of Aram, and its power hit a low point.

For Asia in 835 BCE, “Jehu of Israel dies; Jehoahaz succeeds” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: San Lorenzo in Olmec culture flourishes

summary.en: The Olmec civilization's San Lorenzo site was at its peak. Colossal stone heads (up to 3 meters tall, weighing 20 tons) were transported from quarries tens of kilometers away and carved with African-like features. The Olmecs also built complex drainage systems and artificial earthen pyramids, and invented the earliest Mesoamerican calendar and writing symbols. This 'mother cult

statement.zh: 中美洲奥尔梅克文明（Olmec）的圣洛伦佐（San Lorenzo）遗址正处于鼎盛时期，巨石人头雕像（高达3米，重20吨）从数十公里外的采石场运输至此，雕刻出具有非洲化特征的头像。奥尔梅克人还建造了复杂的排水系统和人工土丘金字塔，发明了最早的中美洲历法和文字符号。这个“母文化”将对后来的玛雅、萨波特克等文明产生深远影响。
statement.en: The Olmec civilization's San Lorenzo site was at its peak.

title.en: Assyrian civil war ends; Shamshi-Adad V ascends

summary.en: The Assyrian civil war ended with victory for Shamshi-Adad V; his elder brother Ashur-danin-apli was defeated and killed. However, the four-year civil war severely weakened the Assyrian Empire. Babylonia, Urartu, and Media regained independence, and Assyria's territory shrank to the core region of Mesopotamia. Shamshi-Adad V had to spend his entire reign restoring order, but th

statement.zh: 亚述王位内战以沙姆希·阿达德五世（Shamshi-Adad V）获胜而告终，其兄长亚述·丹·阿普利战败被杀。然而四年内战使亚述帝国国力严重削弱，巴比伦尼亚、乌拉尔图和米底纷纷独立，亚述疆域退回两河核心区。沙姆希·阿达德五世不得不花费整个在位期来重建秩序，但亚述的鼎盛时代已然暂告段落。
statement.en:
The Assyrian civil war ended with victory for Shamshi-Adad V; his elder brother Ashur-danin-apli was defeated and killed. However, the four-year civil war severely weakened the Assyrian Empire. Babylonia, Urartu, and Media regained independence, and Assyria's territory shrank to the core region of Mesopotamia. Shamshi-Adad V had to spend his entire reign restoring order, but the golden age of Assyria had temporarily ended.

For Asia in 830 BCE, “Assyrian civil war ends; Shamshi-Adad V ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Gonghe Regency ends; King Xuan of Zhou ascends

summary.en: King Li of Zhou, who had fled to Zhi, died. The nobles of the Gonghe Regency returned power to Li's crown prince, Ji Jing, who became King Xuan of Zhou. Having grown up in the home of Duke Mu of Shao, Xuan was well aware of the people's hardships and the lessons of Li's tyranny. After ascending, he worked diligently to restore order, appointing capable ministers such as Duke Mu

statement.zh: 流亡彘地的周厉王去世，共和行政的贵族们还政于厉王的太子姬静，是为周宣王。宣王自幼在召穆公家中长大，深知民生疾苦和厉王暴政的教训。即位后他励精图治，任用召穆公、尹吉甫、仲山甫等贤臣，宣布废除苛捐杂税，恢复“任土作贡”制度，整顿军队，周王室势力有所回升，史称“宣王中兴”。
statement.en:
King Li of Zhou, who had fled to Zhi, died. The nobles of the Gonghe Regency returned power to Li's crown prince, Ji Jing, who became King Xuan of Zhou. Having grown up in the home of Duke Mu of Shao, Xuan was well aware of the people's hardships and the lessons of Li's tyranny. After ascending, he worked diligently to restore order, appointing capable ministers such as Duke Mu of Shao, Yin Jifu, and Zhong Shanfu. He announced the abolition of exorbitant taxes and miscellaneous levies, restored the system of tribute based on land productivity, and reorganized the military. The Zhou royal house regained some strength, a period known as the 'Restoration under King Xuan.'

For Asia in 828 BCE, “Gonghe Regency ends; King Xuan of Zhou ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Accession of King Xuan of Zhou, Ushering in a Revival

summary.en: In 827 BC, Ji Jing ascended the throne as King Xuan of Zhou. Learning from the mistakes of his father, King Li of Zhou, whose oppressive policies had triggered a popular uprising, he appointed capable ministers such as Duke Mu of Shao, Yin Jifu, and Zhong Shanfu, reorganized the court, abolished the harsh laws of King Li's era, and restored the situation where 'all vassals agai

statement.zh: 公元前827年，周宣王姬静继承王位，他吸取父王周厉王因专利暴政引发国人暴动的教训，任用召穆公、尹吉甫、仲山甫等贤臣，整顿朝政，废除厉王时期的苛政，恢复“宣王既立，诸侯复宗周”的局面。宣王在位期间，多次对周边戎狄部落用兵，取得一系列胜利，史称“宣王中兴”，暂时延缓了西周的衰落。
statement.en:
In 827 BC, Ji Jing ascended the throne as King Xuan of Zhou. Learning from the mistakes of his father, King Li of Zhou, whose oppressive policies had triggered a popular uprising, he appointed capable ministers such as Duke Mu of Shao, Yin Jifu, and Zhong Shanfu, reorganized the court, abolished the harsh laws of King Li's era, and restored the situation where 'all vassals again respected the Zhou court'. During his reign, King Xuan launched multiple military campaigns against the Rong and Di tribes, achieving a series of victories, known as the 'Revival under King Xuan', which temporarily delayed the decline of the Western Zhou.

For Asia in 827 BCE, “Accession of King Xuan of Zhou, Ushering in a Revival” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

en: In 827 BC, Ji Jing ascended the throne as King Xuan of Zhou. Learning from the mistakes of his father, King Li of Zhou, whose oppressive policies had triggered a popular uprising, he appointed capable ministers such as Duke Mu of Shao, Yin Jifu, and Zhong Shanfu, reorganized the court, abolished the harsh laws of King Li's era, and restored the situation where 'all vassals again respected the Zhou court'. During his reign, King Xuan launched multiple military campaigns against the Rong and Di tribes, achieving a series of victories, known as the 'Revival under King Xuan', which temporarily delayed the decline of the Western Zhou.
In 827 BC, Ji Jing ascended the throne as King Xuan of Zhou.

statement.zh: 犹太祭司耶何耶大在耶路撒冷圣殿中藏匿了王子约阿施六年，在第七年召集利未人和族长，在圣殿公开拥立7岁的约阿施为王。他们杀死太后亚他利雅，拆毁巴力庙，恢复对雅威的崇拜，并与王立约。约阿施年幼，由耶何耶大摄政，他下令重修圣殿，修复被亚他利雅破坏的墙壁和器具，犹太王室复辟。
statement.en:
Priest Jehoiada had hidden the young prince Joash in the Temple in Jerusalem for six years. In the seventh year, he summoned the Levites and clan heads, publicly proclaimed the 7-year-old Joash as king in the Temple, killing the queen mother Athaliah, demolishing the temple of Baal, and restoring the worship of Yahweh. They made a covenant with the king. Joash was young, and Jehoiada served as regent. He ordered the repair of the Temple, fixing the walls and vessels damaged by Athaliah, restoring the Judean monarchy.

title.en: Early formation of the Median kingdom

summary.en: The Median tribes elected Deioces (according to Herodotus) as king. He built palaces and walls at Ecbatana (present-day Hamadan) and established the Median kingdom. Deioces instituted court rituals, established a system of judges and spies appointed by the king, and transformed the tribal chieftain alliance into a centralized monarchy, laying the foundation for the later Median

statement.zh: 米底人（Medes）各部落推举戴奥凯斯（Deioces，据希罗多德记载）为国王，在埃克巴坦那（今哈马丹）修建宫殿和城墙，建立米底王国。戴奥凯斯设立宫廷礼仪，建立由国王委任的法官和间谍系统，将部落酋长联盟改造为中央集权的君主国，为日后米底帝国扩张奠定基础。历史学家认为米底统一过程持续数十年，但公元前825年前后应是关键节点。
statement.en:
The Median tribes elected Deioces (according to Herodotus) as king. He built palaces and walls at Ecbatana (present-day Hamadan) and established the Median kingdom. Deioces instituted court rituals, established a system of judges and spies appointed by the king, and transformed the tribal chieftain alliance into a centralized monarchy, laying the foundation for the later Median Empire. Historians believe the unification of Media took several decades, but around 825 BCE was a key turning point.

For Asia in 825 BCE, “Early formation of the Median kingdom” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

sources.excerpt: Deioces (flourished late 8th and early 7th centuries bc) was a petty Median chieftain subject to the kingdom of Mannai ... later tradition made him the founder of the Median empire. According to the 5th-century-bc Greek historian Herodotus, Deioces was the first king of the Medes. ... Deioces united all the Median tribes, built Ecbatana (modern Hamadan, Iran) as their capital, and ruled for 53 years (728–675 bc). Modern scholarship has shown that Herodotus probably confused Deioces with Phraortes, who established a kingdom in Media and ruled from about 675 to about 653 bc.

statement.zh: 西北戎狄（包括猃狁和犬戎）联合入侵周朝，周宣王亲自率军在千亩（今山西介休）与戎狄主力决战。战况激烈，周王室军队依靠战车优势勉强取胜，但损失相当数量的“南国之师”。此战虽暂时阻止了戎狄东进，但未能根除边患，此后戎狄仍频繁骚扰。宣王认识到军力不足，开始“料民于太原”，清查户口以扩充兵源。
statement.en:
Northwestern Rong and Di tribes (including the Xianyun and Quanrong) allied to invade Zhou. King Xuan personally led the army to fight them at Qianmu (present-day Jiexiu, Shanxi). The battle was fierce. The Zhou army, relying on chariot advantages, narrowly won, but suffered considerable losses of the 'Southern Army'. Although the battle temporarily halted the Rong-Di advance eastward, it did not eradicate the border threat, and the Rong-Di continued to raid frequently. Recognizing the insufficient military strength, King Xuan began to 'count the people in Taiyuan' (a census) to expand manpower.

For Asia in 825 BCE, “King Xuan of Zhou campaigns against northwestern Rong and Di, battles at Qianmu” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 淮夷和徐夷（今安徽、江苏北部）联合叛周，阻断南方的铜锡运输线“金道锡行”。周宣王命尹吉甫率成周八师和诸侯联军出征，在淮水流域大败徐夷，俘虏其首领，招降了淮夷诸部。铭文记载于“兮甲盘”上，记录了战争过程和缴获，周朝恢复了与南方的青铜原料交通，保证了王室礼器和兵器的铸造。
statement.en:
The Huaiyi and Xuyi (present-day northern Anhui and Jiangsu) allied to rebel against Zhou, blocking the southern copper-tin transport route. King Xuan ordered Yin Jifu to lead the Chengzhou Eight Armies and vassal forces against them. They decisively defeated the Xuyi in the Huai River valley, captured their leader, and induced the Huaiyi tribes to submit. The campaign is recorded on the 'Xi Jia Pan' bronze vessel, describing the battle and booty. Zhou restored contact with the southern source of bronze, ensuring the casting of royal ritual vessels and weapons.

For Asia in 823 BCE, “King Xuan of Zhou campaigns against Huaiyi and Xuyi” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 希腊优卑亚岛的城市卡尔基斯和埃雷特里亚联合在意大利南部的皮提库萨岛（Ischia）建立了首个“大殖民”据点，称为“皮提库萨”。殖民者在此开采铁矿，并与伊特鲁里亚人进行贸易，出土的“内斯特之杯”铭文是最早的希腊字母书写证据之一。这次殖民是希腊殖民运动的先声，此后希腊人开始大规模向西地中海扩张。
statement.en:
The Euboean cities of Chalcis and Eretria jointly established the first 'great colony' at Pithekoussai (Ischia) in southern Italy, called 'Pithekoussai'. The colonists mined iron there and traded with the Etruscans. The 'Cup of Nestor' inscription found there is one of the earliest examples of Greek alphabetic writing. This colony was a precursor to the Greek colonization movement, after which Greeks began large-scale expansion into the western Mediterranean.

title.en: Urartu establishes co-rulership: joint inscriptions of Ishpuini and Menua

summary.en: King Ishpuini of Urartu raised his son Menua to co-ruler; thereafter royal inscriptions were issued jointly in both names, as on the Urartian-Assyrian bilingual stele of Kelishin. The co-regency secured an orderly succession and allowed Urartu to campaign north and south of Lake Van at the same time, laying the basis for more than half a century of ascendancy.

title.en: Founding Carthage: tradition and archaeology

summary.en: Tradition says the Phoenicians of Tyre founded Carthage in 814 BCE and called it 'new town'; the Roman tradition credits Dido, chiefly through the Aeneid. Archaeology has found nothing earlier than the last quarter of the 8th century BCE, about a century later than the tradition, while Utica may be half a century older. Carthage occupied a triangular peninsula on the Gulf of Tu

statement.zh: 根据传统，推罗的腓尼基人于前814年建立迦太基，城名意为“新城”。
statement.en: According to tradition, the Phoenicians of Tyre founded Carthage in 814 BCE; its Phoenician name means 'new town'.

sources.excerpt: According to tradition, Carthage was founded by the Phoenicians of Tyre in 814 BCE; its Phoenician name means “new town.”

zh: 根据传统，推罗的腓尼基人于前814年建立迦太基，城名意为“新城”。
en: According to tradition, the Phoenicians of Tyre founded Carthage in 814 BCE; its Phoenician name means 'new town'.

note.zh: 写“根据传统”，不写“确证于前814年”。
note.en: Says 'according to tradition', not proven in 814 BCE.

statement.zh: 罗马传统把建城归给推罗公主狄多；她因兄弟皮格马利翁而逃离推罗，这个故事因维吉尔的《埃涅阿斯纪》而广为人知。
statement.en: The Roman tradition credits the foundation to the Tyrian princess Dido, who fled from her brother Pygmalion; the story became widely known through Virgil's Aeneid.

sources.excerpt: The Roman tradition is better known, however, because of the Aeneid, which tells of the city’s foundation by the Tyrian princess Dido, who fled from her brother Pygmalion (the name of a historical king of Tyre).

zh: 罗马传统把建城归给推罗公主狄多；她因兄弟皮格马利翁而逃离推罗，这个故事因维吉尔的《埃涅阿斯纪》而广为人知。
en: The Roman tradition credits the foundation to the Tyrian princess Dido, who fled from her brother Pygmalion; the story became widely known through Virgil's Aeneid.

note.zh: 明确标为罗马传统与文学叙事；不写“狄多确有其人”。
note.en: Marked as Roman tradition and literary narrative; no claim that Dido certainly existed.

statement.zh: 狄多叙事不是同时代记录，而是后世罗马文学对建城记忆的重写。
statement.en: The Dido narrative is not a contemporary record but a later Roman literary rewriting of the city's foundation memory.

zh: 狄多叙事不是同时代记录，而是后世罗马文学对建城记忆的重写。
en: The Dido narrative is not a contemporary record but a later Roman literary rewriting of the city's foundation memory.

note.zh: 作者判断：把狄多从史料人物降为文学传统。
note.en: Author judgment: treats Dido as literary tradition, not a historical source.

statement.zh: 传统日期可能被迦太基人自己夸大了；考古没有发现早于前8世纪最后四分之一的东西，比传统建城年代晚了整整一个世纪。
statement.en: The traditional date was probably exaggerated by the Carthaginians themselves; nothing earlier than the last quarter of the 8th century BCE has been found, a full century later than the traditional foundation.

sources.excerpt: The traditional date of the foundation of Carthage as 814 BCE was probably exaggerated by the Carthaginians themselves, for it does not necessarily agree with the archaeological data. Nothing earlier than the last quarter of the 8th century BCE has been discovered, a full century later than the traditional foundation date.

zh: 传统日期可能被迦太基人自己夸大了；考古没有发现早于前8世纪最后四分之一的东西，比传统建城年代晚了整整一个世纪。
en: The traditional date was probably exaggerated by the Carthaginians themselves; nothing earlier than the last quarter of the 8th century BCE has been found, a full century later than the traditional foundation.

note.zh: 考古上限与“可能夸大”照条目；不写“考古证明建城于前814年”。
note.en: Archaeological limit and 'probably exaggerated' follow the entry; no claim that archaeology proves 814 BCE.

statement.zh: 乌提卡可能比迦太基早约半个世纪，说明这一带早有腓尼基据点。
statement.en: Utica may have predated Carthage by about half a century, showing that Phoenician settlements in the region were already older.

sources.excerpt: Carthage was probably not the earliest Phoenician settlement in the region; Utica may have predated it by half a century.

zh: 乌提卡可能比迦太基早约半个世纪，说明这一带早有腓尼基据点。
en: Utica may have predated Carthage by about half a century, showing that Phoenician settlements in the region were already older.

note.zh: 写“可能早约半个世纪”，不写“乌提卡建于前1100年”。
note.en: Says 'may have predated by half a century', not 'Utica founded in 1100 BCE'.

statement.zh: 迦太基建在突尼斯湾海岸的一个三角半岛上，背靠突尼斯湖，靠近西西里海峡，卡住东西地中海航线的瓶颈；古城核心是俯瞰海面的比尔萨卫城。
statement.en: Carthage was built on a triangular peninsula on the Gulf of Tunis, backed by the Lake of Tunis and close to the Strait of Sicily, a strategic bottleneck in east-west Mediterranean trade; its ancient core was the Byrsa citadel overlooking the sea.

sources.excerpt: The site chosen for Carthage in the centre of the shore of the Gulf of Tunis was ideal; the city was built on a triangular peninsula covered with low hills and backed by the Lake of Tunis … its proximity to the Strait of Sicily placed it at a strategic bottleneck in east-west Mediterranean trade. … The ancient citadel, the Byrsa, was on a low hill overlooking the sea.

zh: 迦太基建在突尼斯湾海岸的一个三角半岛上，背靠突尼斯湖，靠近西西里海峡，卡住东西地中海航线的瓶颈；古城核心是俯瞰海面的比尔萨卫城。
en: Carthage was built on a triangular peninsula on the Gulf of Tunis, backed by the Lake of Tunis and close to the Strait of Sicily, a strategic bottleneck in east-west Mediterranean trade; its ancient core was the Byrsa citadel overlooking the sea.

note.zh: 只写选址、湖、海峡与比尔萨；不写“军港可容二百艘战舰”。
note.en: Only the site, lake, strait and Byrsa; no claim that the military harbour held 200 warships.

statement.zh: 迦太基控制西地中海的紫色染料贸易，并经营北非和西班牙南部的银矿：加的斯附近约前800年已开采，前3世纪又开发卡塔赫纳。
statement.en: Carthage controlled much of the western Mediterranean trade in purple dye and drew revenue from silver mines in North Africa and southern Spain: mining near Gadir began as early as 800 BCE, and near Cartagena in the 3rd century BCE.

sources.excerpt: Much of the revenue of Carthage came from its exploitation of the silver mines of North Africa and southern Spain, begun as early as 800 BCE near Gadir (modern Cádiz, Spain) and in the 3rd century BCE near what is now Cartagena, Spain. … Carthage controlled much of the Western trade in the luxurious purple dye from the murex shell.

zh: 迦太基控制西地中海的紫色染料贸易，并经营北非和西班牙南部的银矿：加的斯附近约前800年已开采，前3世纪又开发卡塔赫纳。
en: Carthage controlled much of the western Mediterranean trade in purple dye and drew revenue from silver mines in North Africa and southern Spain: mining near Gadir began as early as 800 BCE, and near Cartagena in the 3rd century BCE.

note.zh: 写紫色染料与银矿收入；不写“迦太基垄断全部西地中海贸易”。
note.en: Purple dye and silver revenue; no claim of a complete monopoly of western Mediterranean trade.

statement.zh: 到前5世纪，迦太基已是西部腓尼基人的领袖，形成以北非为中心的帝国。
statement.en: By the 5th century BCE Carthage had become the leader of the western Phoenicians, forming an empire centred on North Africa.

sources.excerpt: By the 5th century BCE, it had become the leader of the western Phoenicians, forming its own empire centered on North Africa.

zh: 到前5世纪，迦太基已是西部腓尼基人的领袖，形成以北非为中心的帝国。
en: By the 5th century BCE Carthage had become the leader of the western Phoenicians, forming an empire centred on North Africa.

note.zh: 写“领袖”和“以北非为中心”，不写“统一西地中海”。
note.en: Says leader and North-African-centred empire; no claim of unifying the western Mediterranean.

statement.zh: 前146年，罗马在第三次布匿战争中攻破迦太基，城市被掠夺和焚毁。
statement.en: In 146 BCE Rome captured Carthage in the Third Punic War and plundered and burned the city.

sources.excerpt: When Carthage finally fell in 146 BCE, the site was plundered and burned, fulfilling the demand by the senator and orator Cato the Elder … “Carthage must be destroyed.”

zh: 前146年，罗马在第三次布匿战争中攻破迦太基，城市被掠夺和焚毁。
en: In 146 BCE Rome captured Carthage in the Third Punic War and plundered and burned the city.

note.zh: 只写前146年城毁；罗马重建另句带过。
note.en: Only the destruction in 146 BCE; the Roman rebuild is mentioned separately.

statement.zh: 传统日期是城市记忆的一部分，不是考古地层；把两者分开，才能同时保留传说的意义和考古的证据。
statement.en: The traditional date belongs to civic memory, not to an archaeological layer; keeping the two apart preserves both the meaning of the legend and the evidence of the excavator.

zh: 传统日期是城市记忆的一部分，不是考古地层；把两者分开，才能同时保留传说的意义和考古的证据。
en: The traditional date belongs to civic memory, not to an archaeological layer; keeping the two apart preserves both the meaning of the legend and the evidence of the excavator.

note.zh: 作者判断：传统与考古分层，不互相取消。
note.en: Author judgment: tradition and archaeology are kept in separate registers.

title.en: Urartian king Ishpuini conquers Musasir

summary.en: Urartian king Ishpuini led his army to capture Musasir, the sacred city of the Urartian supreme god Haldi. Ishpuini dedicated a large amount of booty to Haldi and erected stone inscriptions in the city. Thereafter, Urartu elevated Haldi as the supreme god, unifying religious belief, enhancing the legitimacy of divine kingship, and strengthening national cohesion.

title.en: Adad-nirari III ascends to Assyrian throne

statement.zh: 希腊克里特岛的城邦开始将习惯法刻在石块或铜板上公之于众，这是希腊最早的法典。法律内容包括审判程序、财产继承和债务纠纷等，标志着城邦政治向法制化迈出了重要一步，平民可以依据公开法律保护自身权利，限制了贵族的随意解释权。
statement.en:
City-states on the island of Crete began to inscribe customary laws on stone or bronze for public display, representing the earliest Greek legal codes. The laws covered judicial procedures, inheritance, and debt disputes, marking an important step toward the rule of law in city-state politics. Commoners could protect their rights based on public laws, limiting the arbitrary interpretation of the aristocracy.

For Europe in 810 BCE, “First written laws appear in Greece” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Assyria captures Damascus, fully conquering Syria

summary.en: After two years of siege, Adad-nirari III finally captured Damascus, sacking it and resettling its inhabitants across Assyria. King Mari of Damascus was captured, humiliated, and executed. Assyria fully incorporated Syria into its provincial system, establishing a garrison governor, controlling all trade routes in the Levant, and strictly supervising the Phoenician city-states.

statement.zh: 亚述国王阿达德尼拉里三世经过两年围攻，最终攻陷大马士革城，将其洗劫一空并将居民迁往亚述各地。大马士革国王马里被俘，受尽侮辱后处死。亚述将叙利亚完全纳入行省体系，设立驻军总督，控制了黎凡特地区的所有贸易路线，并对腓尼基城邦实施严格监督。此次征服标志着亚述帝国达到其鼎盛时期的疆域。

title.en: Rise of the city-state of Athens

summary.en: Theseus is said to have unified Attica's settlements; Athens emerged as a polis that would become the cradle of democracy, philosophy and drama.

statement.zh:
提修斯统一阿提卡诸聚落，雅典作为城邦（polis）兴起，日后成为民主、哲学与戏剧的摇篮。把分散聚落整合为单一政治共同体，是城邦形成的关键一步：它使阿提卡范围内的人口共享同一套政治身份，也为后来的公民大会与公共空间提供了前提。

title.en: The Homeric epics take shape

summary.en: The Iliad and Odyssey fixed in oral form; fount of Western literature

statement.en: Around the eighth century BCE, bards in Ionia shaped songs of the Trojan War and the heroes' return into hexameter epics, giving the Iliad and the Odyssey a relatively fixed form.

title.en: The alphabet: from North Semitic to Greek

summary.en: The Phoenician alphabet developed from the North Semitic alphabet and was spread by Phoenician traders. The earliest surviving inscription is the Ahiram epitaph at Byblos, from the 11th century BCE; the alphabet had 22 signs, ran right to left, represented consonants only, and remained in use in Phoenicia until about the 1st century BCE. Colonial variants included Cypro-Phoenic

statement.zh: 腓尼基字母从北闪米特字母发展而来，由腓尼基商人传播到地中海各地；它是希腊字母的“可能祖先”，也因此成为所有西方字母的远祖。
statement.en: The Phoenician alphabet developed out of the North Semitic alphabet and was spread around the Mediterranean by Phoenician traders; it is the probable ancestor of the Greek alphabet and therefore of all Western alphabets.

sources.excerpt: Phoenician alphabet, writing system that developed out of the North Semitic alphabet and was spread over the Mediterranean area by Phoenician traders. It is the probable ancestor of the Greek alphabet and, hence, of all Western alphabets.

zh: 腓尼基字母从北闪米特字母发展而来，由腓尼基商人传播到地中海各地；它是希腊字母的“可能祖先”，也因此成为所有西方字母的远祖。
en: The Phoenician alphabet developed out of the North Semitic alphabet and was spread around the Mediterranean by Phoenician traders; it is the probable ancestor of the Greek alphabet and therefore of all Western alphabets.

note.zh: 明确写“从北闪米特发展”和“可能祖先”；不写“腓尼基人凭空创造22字母”。
note.en: Says development from North Semitic and 'probable ancestor'; no claim of inventing 22 letters from nothing.

statement.en: The earliest surviving Phoenician inscription is the Ahiram epitaph at Byblos, dating from the 11th century BCE. It is written in the North Semitic alphabet.

sources.excerpt: The earliest Phoenician inscription that has survived is the Ahiram epitaph at Byblos in Phoenicia, dating from the 11th century BCE and written in the North Semitic alphabet.

zh: 现存最早的腓尼基铭文，是比布鲁斯国王阿希拉姆的墓志，属前11世纪。它用北闪米特字母书写。
en: The earliest surviving Phoenician inscription is the Ahiram epitaph at Byblos, dating from the 11th century BCE. It is written in the North Semitic alphabet.

note.zh: 只写墓志年代与字体；不写“阿希拉姆墓志就是成熟腓尼基字母”。
note.en: Only the epitaph's date and script; no claim that it is already the mature Phoenician alphabet.

statement.zh: 这套字母只有22个符号，从右向左写，只表辅音。
statement.en: The alphabet had only 22 signs, written from right to left and representing consonants alone.

sources.excerpt: The alphabet remained, however, essentially a Semitic alphabet of 22 letters, written from right to left, with only consonants represented and phonetic values unchanged from the North Semitic script.

zh: 这套字母只有22个符号，从右向左写，只表辅音。
en: The alphabet had only 22 signs, written from right to left and representing consonants alone.

note.zh: 字母数、方向与辅音照条目；不写“没有元音就不能读”。
note.en: Letter count, direction and consonants follow the entry; no claim that vowels made reading impossible.

statement.zh: 在腓尼基本土，它一直用到约前1世纪。
statement.en: In Phoenicia proper it remained in use until about the 1st century BCE.

sources.excerpt: … was in use until about the 1st century BCE in Phoenicia proper.

zh: 在腓尼基本土，它一直用到约前1世纪。
en: In Phoenicia proper it remained in use until about the 1st century BCE.

note.zh: 只写本土使用下限；布匿与后布匿另条。
note.en: Only the mainland limit; Punic and neo-Punic are treated separately.

statement.zh: 塞浦路斯—腓尼基字母用于前10–前2世纪，撒丁字母约在前9世纪；第三支变体在迦太基演化为布匿字母和后布匿字母，一直写到约3世纪。
statement.en: Cypro-Phoenician was used from the 10th to the 2nd century BCE and Sardinian around the 9th century; a third variant evolved at Carthage into Punic and neo-Punic, written until about the 3rd century CE.

sources.locator: Britannica, Phoenician alphabet, colonial scripts paragraph
sources.excerpt: Phoenician colonial scripts … are classified as Cypro-Phoenician (10th–2nd century BCE) and Sardinian (c. 9th century BCE) varieties. A third variety … evolved into the Punic and neo-Punic alphabets of Carthage, which continued to be written until about the 3rd century CE.

zh: 塞浦路斯—腓尼基字母用于前10–前2世纪，撒丁字母约在前9世纪；第三支变体在迦太基演化为布匿字母和后布匿字母，一直写到约3世纪。
en: Cypro-Phoenician was used from the 10th to the 2nd century BCE and Sardinian around the 9th century; a third variant evolved at Carthage into Punic and neo-Punic, written until about the 3rd century CE.

note.zh: 殖民变体与布匿/后布匿照条目；不写“布匿字母就是腓尼基字母原样”。
note.en: Colonial variants and Punic/neo-Punic follow the entry; no claim that Punic was identical to the mainland script.

statement.zh: 希腊字母约在前1000年形成，经腓尼基字母从北闪米特字母衍生；希腊人把几个只表辅音的符号改成元音。
statement.en: The Greek alphabet formed about 1000 BCE, derived from the North Semitic alphabet via the Phoenicians; the Greeks turned several consonantal signs into vowels.

sources.excerpt: The Greek alphabet is a writing system that was developed in Greece about 1000 BCE. … It was derived from the North Semitic alphabet via that of the Phoenicians. … some of the symbols of the Semitic alphabet, which represented only consonants, were made to represent vowels …

zh: 希腊字母约在前1000年形成，经腓尼基字母从北闪米特字母衍生；希腊人把几个只表辅音的符号改成元音。
en: The Greek alphabet formed about 1000 BCE, derived from the North Semitic alphabet via the Phoenicians; the Greeks turned several consonantal signs into vowels.

note.zh: 写“经腓尼基字母衍生”和“辅音符号改元音”；不写“希腊人从零发明元音”。
note.en: Says derivation via the Phoenician alphabet and consonantal signs turned into vowels; no claim that Greeks invented vowels from nothing.

statement.zh: alef、he、yod、ayin、vav 变成 alpha、epsilon、iota、omicron、upsilon。
statement.en: Alef, he, yod, ayin and vav became alpha, epsilon, iota, omicron and upsilon.

sources.excerpt: … the Semitic consonants ʾalef, he, yod, ʿayin, and vav became the Greek letters alpha, epsilon, iota, omicron, and upsilon, representing the vowels a, e, i, o, and u, respectively.

zh: alef、he、yod、ayin、vav 变成 alpha、epsilon、iota、omicron、upsilon。
en: Alef, he, yod, ayin and vav became alpha, epsilon, iota, omicron and upsilon.

note.zh: 只列字母对应；不写“五个符号全部变成元音字母”以外的推论。
note.en: Only the letter correspondences; no inference beyond the five signs becoming vowel letters.

statement.zh: 西部希腊字母又经伊特鲁里亚字母传给拉丁字母。
statement.en: The western Greek alphabet passed through Etruscan to Latin.

sources.locator: Britannica, Greek alphabet, Etruscan and Latin
sources.excerpt: The Chalcidian alphabet probably gave rise to the Etruscan alphabet of Italy in the 8th century BCE and hence indirectly to the other Italic alphabets, including the Latin.

zh: 西部希腊字母又经伊特鲁里亚字母传给拉丁字母。
en: The western Greek alphabet passed through Etruscan to Latin.

note.zh: 写“经伊特鲁里亚间接传给拉丁”；不写“拉丁字母直接复制希腊字母”。
note.en: Says Etruscan indirect route to Latin; no claim that Latin copied Greek directly.

statement.zh: 字母史的要点不是“谁第一个发明”，而是“谁让一套符号足够简单，能被不同语言反复借用和改写”。
statement.en: The point of alphabet history is not who invented it first, but who made a set of signs simple enough to be borrowed and rewritten by different languages.

zh: 字母史的要点不是“谁第一个发明”，而是“谁让一套符号足够简单，能被不同语言反复借用和改写”。
en: The point of alphabet history is not who invented it first, but who made a set of signs simple enough to be borrowed and rewritten by different languages.

note.zh: 作者判断：把字母史从发明权争夺改成传播与适配。
note.en: Author judgment: shifts alphabet history from invention claims to diffusion and adaptation.

title.en: Rise of Carthage as the Hegemon of the Western Mediterranean

summary.en: Around 800 BC, Phoenician colonists from Tyre founded Carthage (near present-day Tunis) in North Africa. Carthage exploited its advantageous geographic position to control western Mediterranean trade, rapidly developing into a maritime empire. Carthaginians conducted a circumnavigation of Africa (c. 600 BC) and established trading posts in West Africa, exchanging gold, ivory, a

statement.zh: 约公元前800年，腓尼基推罗城邦的殖民者在北非建立迦太基（Carthage，今突尼斯）。迦太基利用其优越的地理位置控制西地中海贸易，迅速发展为海上帝国。迦太基人进行环非洲航行（约前600年），在西非建立了贸易站，与当地部落交换黄金、象牙和奴隶。迦太基最终在布匿战争（前264-146年）中被罗马毁灭，但其非洲领地成为罗马阿非利加行省。
statement.en:
Around 800 BC, Phoenician colonists from Tyre founded Carthage (near present-day Tunis) in North Africa. Carthage exploited its advantageous geographic position to control western Mediterranean trade, rapidly developing into a maritime empire. Carthaginians conducted a circumnavigation of Africa (c. 600 BC) and established trading posts in West Africa, exchanging gold, ivory, and slaves with local tribes. Carthage was eventually destroyed by Rome in the Punic Wars (264-146 BC), and its African territories became the Roman province of Africa.

For Africa in 800 BCE, “Rise of Carthage as the Hegemon of the Western Mediterranean” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 约公元前800年，腓尼基推罗城邦的殖民者在北非建立迦太基（Carthage，今突尼斯）。迦太基利用其优越的地理位置控制西地中海贸易，迅速发展为海上帝国。迦太基人进行环非洲航行（约前600年），在西非建立了贸易站，与当地部落交换黄金、象牙和奴隶。迦太基最终在布匿战争（前264-146年）中被罗马毁灭，但其非洲领地成为罗马阿非利加行省。
约公元前800年，腓尼基推罗城邦的殖民者在北非建立迦太基（Carthage，今突尼斯）。
en: Around 800 BC, Phoenician colonists from Tyre founded Carthage (near present-day Tunis) in North Africa. Carthage exploited its advantageous geographic position to control western Mediterranean trade, rapidly developing into a maritime empire. Carthaginians conducted a circumnavigation of Africa (c. 600 BC) and established trading posts in West Africa, exchanging gold, ivory, and slaves with local tribes. Carthage was eventually destroyed by Rome in the Punic Wars (264-146 BC), and its African territories became the Roman province of Africa.
Around 800 BC, Phoenician colonists from Tyre founded Carthage (near present-day Tunis) in North Africa.

statement.zh: 迦太基约于公元前814年由推罗腓尼基人建立，位于突尼斯沿海岬角，凭港口与贸易迅速发展为西地中海主要海上与商业强国，并成为罗马的竞争对手。
statement.en: Carthage was founded by Phoenicians from Tyre about 814 BCE on a promontory on the Tunisian coast; it grew into a thriving port and the chief maritime and commercial power of the western Mediterranean, becoming a rival of Rome.

sources.locator: Opening paragraphs and section on Phoenician colonization
sources.excerpt: Carthage, great city of antiquity on the north coast of Africa, now a residential suburb of the city of Tunis, Tunisia. Built on a promontory on the Tunisian coast, it was placed to influence and control ships passing between Sicily and the North African coast ... Rapidly becoming a thriving port and trading centre, it eventually developed into a major Mediterranean power and a rival to Rome. According to tradition, Carthage was founded by the Phoenicians of Tyre in 814 bce ... Carthage became the chief maritime and commercial power in the western Mediterranean.

zh: 约公元前800年，腓尼基推罗城邦的殖民者在北非建立迦太基（Carthage，今突尼斯）。
en: Around 800 BC, Phoenician colonists from Tyre founded Carthage (near present-day Tunis) in North Africa.

note.zh: 来源记传统建城年为前814年、迦太基为西地中海主要海上商业强国并与罗马竞争，未记环非洲航行与西非贸易站；claim 用前814年，不写约前800年之外的航行细节。
note.en: The source gives the traditional foundation date of 814 BCE, Carthage as the chief maritime and commercial power of the western Mediterranean, and its rivalry with Rome, but not the circumnavigation of Africa or West African trading posts; the claim uses 814 BCE and omits those voyages.
